### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /profile — 5cr

Returns public profile information for a LinkedIn user including name, headline, summary, location, current company, education, skills, and profile picture URL.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the LinkedIn profile page

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /company — 5cr

Returns public information about a LinkedIn company page. Canonical fields carry the identity and reach: `author.id` (the numeric company_id the other `/company/*` endpoints take), `username`, `display_name`, `bio` (the company description), `avatar_url` (logo), `followers`, `location` (flattened HQ), and `verified`. The complete **About tab** rides in `author.ext`: `website`, `employee_count` and `employee_count_range`, `founded_year`, `specialities[]`, `industries[]`, `headquarters` (structured `{country, city, geographic_area, line1, line2, postal_code}`), `locations[]` (every office LinkedIn lists, with lat/long), `hashtags[]`, `cover_url`, and `page_active`. Fields a page has not filled in come back null rather than omitted, so `founded_year` is null on a company that never set a founding date. `funding` is mapped too, but LinkedIn returned an empty funding block for every company measured on 2026-08-11, so do not depend on it.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the LinkedIn company page

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/company?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post — 5cr

Returns detailed information about a specific LinkedIn post including the post text, like count, comment count, share count, author info, media attachments, and publish timestamp.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the LinkedIn post

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/post?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search/people — 10cr

Searches LinkedIn members by name and B2B filters (title, current/past company, school, industry, location, language). Returns a paginated list of matching profiles with handle, headline, location, follower count, and the member URN for follow-up enrichment calls.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Name or display-name keyword to search for (e.g. 'Bill Gates').
- `page` *(optional)*: Page number for pagination (default 1). Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `first_name` *(optional)*: Filter by first name.
- `last_name` *(optional)*: Filter by last name.
- `title` *(optional)*: Filter by job title or headline.
- `current_company` *(optional)*: Filter by current company ID (comma-separated for multiple).
- `past_company` *(optional)*: Filter by a previously-worked company ID.
- `school` *(optional)*: Filter by school ID.
- `industry` *(optional)*: Filter by industry ID.
- `geocode_location` *(optional)*: Filter by location geocode ID.
- `profile_language` *(optional)*: Filter by profile language (ISO 2-letter code, e.g. 'en').
- `service_category` *(optional)*: Filter by service-category ID.
- `follower_of` *(optional)*: Return people who follow a specific member URN.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/search/people?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/about — 5cr

Returns LinkedIn's account-freshness panel for a member: `joined` (the month the account was created) plus how recently the contact information and profile photo were updated. **This is not the member's About/summary section** — despite the resource name, no free-text profile summary is returned, and the upstream does not expose one. The closest public text LinkedIn publishes for a member is the headline, on `author.bio` from `/v1/linkedin/profile`. For a company's About tab, use `/v1/linkedin/company` (`author.ext`).

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the LinkedIn profile, company, or post.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/about?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the LinkedIn profile, company, or post.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/contact?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /company/posts — 5cr

Returns recent posts from a LinkedIn company page. Each post includes text, reaction count, comment count, and media.

**Parameters**

- `company_id`: LinkedIn numeric company ID (from /v1/linkedin/company).
- `page` *(optional)*: Page number for pagination (default 1). Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Post ordering: 'top' or 'recent'.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/company/posts?company_id=<company_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /ad — 5cr

Returns detailed information about a specific LinkedIn advertisement including ad copy, sponsor info, impressions, and targeting.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the LinkedIn ad

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/ad?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /ads/search — 5cr

Searches the LinkedIn Ad Library for ads by company, keyword, or filters. Returns matching ads with ad copy and sponsor info.

**Parameters**

- `company` *(optional)*: The company name to search for. 'Microsoft' for example
- `keyword` *(optional)*: The keyword to search for
- `companyId` *(optional)*: The company id to search for
- `countries` *(optional)*: Comma separated list of countries. Example: US,CA,MX
- `startDate` *(optional)*: Start date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `endDate` *(optional)*: End date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `paginationToken` *(optional)*: Pagination token to paginate through results Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `paginationToken` (cursor style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/ads/search" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search/posts — 5cr

Finds public LinkedIn posts, feed updates, and Pulse articles via Google Search. Returns description, author, media, like count, comment count, and published date when LinkedIn exposes them publicly. Best-effort against Google's index, not a complete native LinkedIn search. Use `date_posted` to narrow to recent posts and forward `cursor` for pagination.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Keyword or phrase to search for in public LinkedIn posts.
- `page` *(optional)*: page Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: sort_by
- `date_posted` *(optional)*: Date filter based on Google-indexed results. One of `past_24h`, `past_week`, `past_month` (underscores, not hyphens).
- `content_type` *(optional)*: content_type
- `from_company` *(optional)*: from_company
- `from_member` *(optional)*: from_member
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/search/posts?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post/transcript — 10cr

Fetches the transcript from a LinkedIn post video when LinkedIn exposes one publicly. Returns `transcript: null` with `transcriptNotAvailable: true` if the post has no transcript — credits are only deducted when a transcript is actually returned.

> ⛔ **BANNED in this plugin: 10 credits, no advantage. Transcribe with the local captions→Groq→Whisper chain instead.**

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the LinkedIn post to transcribe.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/post/transcript?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/full — 5cr

Fans out to the LinkedIn company profile and recent-posts endpoints in parallel and returns the unified author, the recent-post list, and computed metrics — average engagement rate, posting cadence (with the window it was measured over), the top post, and the format mix. The profile leg is the only critical leg: if posts can't be fetched the call still returns the profile with post-dependent metrics null, and every leg's status is surfaced in legs[]. Flat 5 credits.

**Parameters**

- `url` *(optional)*: url
- `posts` *(optional)*: How many recent posts to fetch + average the computed metrics over (1–100, default 25).
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Pass a prior response's posts_cursor to deepen the post window.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of posts,computed (default both). include=computed drops the raw posts[] to save payload.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/full" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a LinkedIn endpoint

⚠️ **LinkedIn has no 1cr tier for content.** Profile, company and post are all **5 credits**
here, against 1cr on every other social platform, and the search endpoints are **10**. Only
three lookup helpers are 1cr. Budget accordingly — a casual "just check their profile" costs
five times what it does on Instagram.

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Resolve a location / school / industry to an id | `/search/location` · `/search/schools` · `/search/industry` | 1 |
| A member's profile | `/profile` | 5 |
| A company page | `/company` | 5 |
| One post | `/post` | 5 |
| A member's posts / comments / reactions | `/profile/posts` · `/profile/comments` · `/profile/reactions` | 5 |
| Follower + connection counts | `/profile/stats` | 5 |
| CV detail (experience, education, skills, certs…) | `/profile/experiences` · `/educations` · `/skills` · `/certifications` … | 5 each |
| Company posts / affiliated pages / insights | `/company/posts` · `/company/affiliated-pages` · `/company/insights` | 5 |
| Ads a company is running | `/ads/search` · `/ad` | 5 |
| Search public posts by keyword | `/search/posts` | 5 |
| **Search people** | `/search/people` | **10** |
| **People at a company** | `/company/people` | **10** |
| **Who reacted to a post** | `/post/reactions` | **10** |
| **Jobs** | `/search/jobs` · `/company/jobs` | **10** |
| ~~Transcript~~ | ⛔ `/post/transcript` is **banned** | — |

### Resolve with the 1cr helpers before any 10cr search

`/search/location`, `/search/schools` and `/search/industry` (1cr each) exist to turn a
human name into the id that the expensive search endpoints require. Guessing the id and
firing `/search/people` (10cr) at it is how you pay 10 credits for an empty result.

### The CV endpoints are individually billed

Experience, education, skills, honors, certifications, publications, volunteers,
recommendations and interests are each their own 5cr call. Reconstructing a full CV is 40+
credits. Pull only the sections the question needs — or take `/profile` (5cr) first and check
whether it already answers it.

## Field Maps


The `profile` and `company` endpoints both return an `Author` response normalized by the `linkedin-author` field map, and `post` returns a `Post` normalized by `linkedin-post`. Both include computed fields under `data.computed`. Use `?format=raw` to bypass both.
